analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/NemotronSuperMediaChargeTests.swift and NemotronSuperServingPolicyTests.swift). No production source is in this batch, so nothing here changes runtime security behavior directly.

MediaChargeTests: the expected error for an oversized body in encodedHeaderQuote changes from invalidInput to bodyTooLarge (head line 42). A new test, bodyBoundHoldsOneSharedIngestPart (head 59-74), checks that a body carrying a MediaIngest.maxMediaDecodedBytes video part passes the ingress bound. It also checks that localInferenceMaxUploadBytes and CoordinatorClient.maxInboundMessageBytes stay at or below Policy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes. This tightens regression coverage on the ingress size bound, which is relevant to the availability and DoS surface (TB-002, TB-007). The expected media charge for 1 image rises from 3,888,385,020 to 5,012,458,492 and for 16 images from 26,317,356,540 to 27,441,430,012 (head 114-115). That implies the production policy now reserves more media memory per request. This is conservative for admission and not a weakening.

ServingPolicyTests: the expected default prefix-bank sizes shrink (10<<28 and 32<<28 instead of 12<<28 and 34<<28; 21<<29 and 27<<28 instead of 22<<29 and 29<<28). That is consistent with the larger media charge being subtracted from the grant. A smaller bank reduces the at-rest and cross-tenant prefix-cache exposure (T-041) and does not widen it. The 16 GiB cap and the 60 GiB-and-up sizes are unchanged.

The production changes behind these expectations (the media charge, maximumEncodedBodyBytes, the bodyTooLarge failure and the ingress limits) are outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm that the policy source matches these test values and that the transports enforce the ingress bound before allocation. I found no concrete regression.
